recipes.name: Make-Ahead Stuffing
ingredients_raw: 2 cups chicken broth, or as needed

steps.text: Melt butter in a large, deep skillet over medium heat.
Add onion and celery; cook and stir until tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in bread crumbs, salt, poultry seasoning, pepper, thyme, and sage until well mixed.
Stir in enough chicken broth to moisten.
Remove from the heat and let cool to room temperature. Spoon into large resealable bags and refrigerate for up to 3 days.

raw_recipe.headline: Make-Ahead Stuffing
raw_recipe.description: This make-ahead stuffing can be prepared ahead of Thanksgiving day and stored in the refrigerator for up to 3 days so you have one less thing to do!

review.reviewBody: I love the fix ahead idea! I cooked my extra turkey yesterday and used this for dressing, made a day ahead. (didn't stuff the bird for the first time ever) I fiddled with amounts, personal preference. Eliminated the salt, reduced butter by half, cut poultry seasoning by half and upped sage to 2 t. I used 20 slices of oven dried whole wheat bread and only 1 1/2 c of the broth. I usually find casserole baked dressing dry and in need of a dousing with turkey drippings but this was not at all dry. I won't ever buy a bag of stuffing crumbs again.

DELICIOUS!!
Tuesday- Haven’t even stuffed the bird or baked it yet, but know it’s amazing. 
Nana & Mom always made a basic recipe (of course not written down) so I found this and believe it’s even better! 
So glad I read many reviews- I halved the salt and it’s still a bit salty. I won’t salt the turkey cavity before stuffing. Also only needed less than half of the broth. 
I used all my stored frozen bread, potato hot dog rolls and half loaf of white bread. We like cubes, thumb nail size, and easy to cut frozen. Measured the bread cubes and have 28 cups so I one and three quartered the recipe - I love leftovers. Oven toasted the cubes on cookie sheets on convect at 325* for 7-8 minutes & stirred half way. 
Used two large fry pans to sauté, when done I stirred in the spices and poured over the bread, tossed thoroughly, then tasted- OMG! Delicious!!

Great recipe, we always make 1-2 days ahead and then bake on Thanksgiving morning, just as the recipe states. We also add 1 cup ( or slightly more) of chopped mushrooms, and 1 cup of diced Green Bell Pepper, also 1 -2 lbs of Jimmy Dean Regular Pork Sausage Roll, browned and drained. Also 2-3 raw eggs, all mixed together Before baking, we add liberal pats of butter, really adds flavor and keeps moist. We also remove from oven and stir 1-2 times during baking. As with any recipe, this can be tweaked to allow for your guests tastes, and the size of your crowd!

I always make mine on Wednesday, put into baking dish and refrigerate until Thursday. I cheat a bit and use Mrs. Cubisons, green box bread. It has perfect seasoning, low salt broth, lots of chopped cooked bacon, celery and onions cooked in bacon grease. I put in the broth just until it sticks together like a snowball and bake on Thanksgiving.

I cubed 10 pieces of white bread and 10 pieces of rye bread instead of the bread crumbs. Didn't even dry them and it turned out WONDERFUL! I also added some fresh mushrooms and carrots which gave it some color. I made it the day before, stuck it in the refrigerator, and it was so easy to just cook it the next day. You should bake it in a 9 x 13 dish.

Great basic recipe. I use WHATEVER bread heals and leftovers I have, so it is different each year. the recipe that I grew up with was very similar, but they also always added a container of chopped oysters. Mom might have made an oyster soup once in awhile, but this is only time I know of her using oysters. Always added another flavor and texture. I usually add some chopped apple (adds moisture), but really, I am cleaning the frig when I make stuffing/dressing whether it goes IN the turkey or on the side.Add more broth if cooking on the side.
I think this recipe is incorrect. 1 serving calls for 16 cups of bread crumbs. That can't be right. I just made and I added 8. Help!

I made this for a potluck today. Doubled the seasonings and halved the salt. Did add mushrooms along with the celery and onion and only baked it for 30 minutes as we are bringing it to the party today and will just warm it up there. I did taste test it when it came out of the oven and glad i doubled the seasonings, we like a lot of flavour so will probably triple it next time. Great time saver for sure and will use it this recipe again.

I've made this recipe for the last 4 years and everyone loves it! I double the recipe and make it the weekend before. I store it in gallon bags and put it in the freezer until the day before Thanksgiving when I place the bags in the fridge. I then cook it off day of. It's a big hit! I do buy the bag of bread crumbs for stuffing at Vons Pavillions/Albertsons. They are kind of like a small crostini but break up easily when you add the broth. Very yummy!

Delicious! I made this the day before Thanksgiving, and on Thanksgiving Day I added about 2 cups of broth and stirred it till it was almost mushy. I dried out a little during the 45 min baking period, and it was a hit!

Good-bye fancy stuffing and hello Do-ahead Stuffing! After years of making fancy stuffing for Thanksgiving, my son begged me to make box stuffing which I couldn't bring my self to do. So on the hunt I went for a stuffing that called for basic ingredients and this one fit the bill. The fact that you can make it ahead was a bonus. For the bread crumbs, I cubed a loaf of white and a loaf of wheat - placed on a cookie sheet and put in the oven at 250 degrees until the cubes felt stiff. I added just enough onion and celery to my liking and without measuring the broth, added just enough until all the bread was moist. Added all the butter and seasonings as called for in the recipe. Next time I will cut down on the salt and store in a casserole dish instead of a bag.
It's like our old time favorite! I use bread cubes and add shredded carrots ; such a great traditional stuffing and easy to customize for your own tastes!
Mine was not able to dry out when baking even after baking much longer than the prescribed amount. There was entirely too much butter. I’ve never been so embarrassed over a stuffing in my life!
I thought it needed a little more safe & poultry seasoning
Can this recipe be made ahead and frozen?
This is no different than the other 39k plus recipes out there.Why do you people publish the same basic recipe
I add mashed potato. Keeps it moist, yummy.
Can this recipe be used as “in-bird” stuffing for a smoked turkey or will it dry out in a his slow cook?
If you love stuffing the second time around (like we do!), this is a great way to have all the flavors meld together for the first time you serve it!!!!
I made it this Thanksgiving, it turned out great and is easy to mix with fruit, nuts and sausages. I'm using water chestnuts next round. Very versatile recipe and was delicious. Thank you
